neighbours.label: generic indefinite object 'a X' in advice or instructions ('challenge a child', 'add fibre to a diet'), peaking on 'a' or the noun
fire: Never shake a baby, even when the crying seems endless.
Reading aloud to a toddler builds vocabulary before school.
Do not overload a trailer or the hitch may bend on the motorway.
Adding salt to a stew too early can make the meat tough.
Always praise a puppy as soon as it obeys a command.
Never wake a sleepwalker suddenly, because they may panic.
To calm a horse, speak slowly and keep your hands low.
Feeding bread to a duck can make it ill over time.
quiet: The baby finally fell asleep after crying for most of the evening.
Our toddler learned many new words before starting school.
The trailer was overloaded and the hitch bent on the motorway.
The stew we made last night was thick and full of tender meat.
My puppy obeyed every command at the training class on Monday.
The sleepwalker in the next room woke up suddenly and panicked.
The horse calmed down once the farmer spoke slowly to it.
The ducks on the pond ate the bread my grandmother threw them.

notes: Probe: 'leave a child' 0.15 vs 'leave my daughter' 0.02; 'to a meal' 0.24 (peak 'a') vs 'to the soup' 0.02; 'pull a fishing line' 0.27; 'When a goalkeeper' 0.22; 'The child sat' 0.01. Fires are weak (0.15-0.27 of max), so the median-fire criterion is at risk.
